comment: Derived-file rules for the auto-resolver's deterministic pre-pass. A file listed in a rule's `owns` is GENERATED, so a merge conflict in it is never a question for a human or a model — the answer is to merge the sources and re-run the generator. .github/scripts/resolve-generated.mjs reads this file; auto-resolve/prepare.sh uses it to route generated conflicts away from the LLM, and to defer the ones whose sources also conflicted until after those sources are resolved. The template ships this file with an empty `rules` array; a repo that DELETES it rather than emptying it loses the pre-pass silently, because an absent config and an empty one mean the same thing to the oracle.

schema.command: argv array to run, from the repo root. Exactly one of `command` or `generator`.
schema.generator: path to a script to run. `interpreter` (argv array) defaults to ["node"].
schema.sources: exact paths whose change requires re-running this rule.
schema.sourcesPattern: optional regex (string) matched against changed paths, in addition to `sources`.
schema.owns: exact paths this rule GENERATES. A conflict in one of these is resolved by regenerating, never by editing.
schema.ownsPrefix: optional path prefix, ending in '/', whose whole subtree this rule generates.
schema.reviewOmit: optional boolean, default false. TRUE asserts that a REQUIRED check re-derives every path this rule owns and fails on any difference, so the committed bytes cannot disagree with their sources. .github/scripts/strip-generated-diff.mjs omits only these paths from the PR reviewer's diff, and the resolver's remerge-diff-report.py reads the same flag through `resolve-generated.mjs --owned --rederived-only` to decide which merge deltas it stops reading. Set it only beside the name of the check that proves it: a path that is merely machine-written (a lockfile) but that no check regenerates and compares stays VISIBLE, because a reviewer is then the only thing reading it.

notOwned.comment: Generated artifacts deliberately left OUT of `rules`, so the next reader does not read their absence as an oversight. A rule that cannot resolve the conflict it claims is worse than no rule: prepare.sh routes the path away from the model on the strength of the claim.
notOwned.python/agent_sanitizer/_bundled/: git-ignored (see .gitignore), so it can never carry a conflict.
notOwned.src/cf-charset.mjs: git-ignored, generated at install time by scripts/gen-unicode.mjs (as are src/joining-type.mjs, src/standardized-variants.mjs, src/unicode-properties.mjs and python/agent_sanitizer/data/invisible-charset.json). src/vendor/gfm-autolink-literal.mjs is git-ignored too, generated by scripts/gen-gfm-autolink.mjs from scripts/patches/, so it can never carry a conflict.
notOwned.CHANGELOG.md: written by scripts/version-bump.sh from the Conventional Commit subjects since the last tag, for one release. There is no generator to re-run over a merge: the resolution is the union of two releases' sections, which is a textual merge the model handles.
notOwned.plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json: its version field is bumped by the same release workflow, and every other field is hand-written — a rule would claim the whole file to regenerate one line.
notOwned.plugin/dist/: git-ignored build output of the plugin, as are plugin/requirements.in and plugin/scripts/lib/{fail-open,node-floor}.sh (plugin/scripts/baked-artifacts.mjs lists them all). Only the release bake commits them, onto the plugin-dist branch, so no branch a merge runs on carries them.
notOwned.plugin/requirements.txt: compiled by plugin/scripts/lock-redactor-deps.mjs, which resolves the dependency tree over the NETWORK — and re-resolving on a merge would float every transitive pin, which is the drift the lock exists to stop. The Required plugin/test/lock-redactor-deps.test.mjs fails when the lock was not compiled from the current `secrets` extra; the fix is a deliberate re-lock, reviewed as a diff.
